One exercise. Four different goals. 

The Bulgarian Split Squat is one of the most versatile movements you can add to your training. Here's how to use it depending on what you're chasing:

⚡️ POWER — Explosive Jump Split Squat
Drive through your front foot and launch off the ground. This trains your fast-twitch muscle fibers and builds the explosive force needed for sprinting, jumping, and athletic performance.

🟡 STABILITY — Isometric Hold with Arm Reach
Hold the bottom position and slowly reach your arms forward and back to practice pure balance work. This builds hip stability and improves proprioception. 

🔴 STRENGTH — Weighted Single-Arm Dumbbell
Add load and slow it down. The single dumbbell forces your core to fight lateral lean while your quads and glutes are under maximum tension. This is your go-to for building size and lower-body strength.

🔵 JOINT HEALTH — Bodyweight Full Range of Motion
No weight, no rush. Move through the deepest range you can control. This lubricates the knee and hip joints, conditions your tendons, and keeps your body feeling good long term.

Start where your nervous system feels safe and then build momentum into a program you can sustain.

🚨 GYMTIMIDATION IS REAL… BUT YOU CAN OVERCOME IT! 💪🏾✨

Ever walked into the gym and felt out of place, unsure, or intimidated? You’re not alone! Today on Breakfast Television, I joined @devobrown to talk about how to create your comfort zone at the gym and step in with confidence.

🔥 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
✅ Start Small & Stick to a Plan – Having a simple, go-to routine eliminates hesitation and builds momentum. Going into the gym with a plan, increases confidence and can reduce anxiety.  Even if it’s just 10 minutes of movement, consistency helps build confidence!
✅ Exposure Therapy – The more you expose yourself to an environment, the safer it feels. Simply showing up regularly—even if it’s just to stretch or walk on the treadmill—trains your brain to recognize the gym as a familiar, safe space.
✅ Box Breathing for Calm & Focus – Spend 2 minutes in your car before walking in: Inhale for 4 sec, hold for 4 sec, exhale for 4 sec, hold for 4 sec. This stimulates your parasympathetic nervous system, reducing anxiety and helping you walk in feeling in control.
✅ Take a Tour, Join a Small Group, or Hire a Trainer – Familiarizing yourself with the space, learning equipment, and getting guidance builds confidence and competence—making the gym feel like home!

💡 Bonus Tips:
➕ Power Posing = Instant Confidence Boost – Stand tall, chest open, hands on hips for 2 minutes before heading in (think Superman/Wonder-woman pose). This can provide feelings of self confidence and can help reduce stress!
➕ Own Your Space – Good posture and open body language change how you feel AND how others perceive you.

The gym is for EVERYONE—so don’t let intimidation hold you back! Walk in like you belong… because you do!
